name: trama
description: See your System as a layered Model of state machines, review Proposals and Drifts, and steer your coding agent from one editor tab.

trama.agentCommand.markdownDescription: Command that starts your coding agent in a terminal. `{prompt}` is replaced by the shell-quoted prompt; if it is missing, the prompt is appended. Examples: `claude {prompt}`, `codex {prompt}`. Trama never calls a model itself.

enumDescriptions: Run `#trama.agentCommand#` in a terminal (omp, claude, codex, copilot CLI, cursor-agent…).
Send the prompt to the agent chat built into the editor (Copilot in VS Code). In Cursor, or if the chat is not available, the prompt is copied to the clipboard.
trama.agentLauncher.markdownDescription: Where the Design, Scan and Run buttons send their prompt.

trama.autoScan.markdownDescription: After you approve a Proposal, launch the agent to Scan the Features it touched. With the terminal launcher it only applies when `#trama.agentCommand#` is set.

trama.skillsDir.markdownDescription: Folder, relative to the project root, where **Trama: Initialize Project** installs the agent skills. Use `.claude/skills` for Claude Code.

languageModelTools.name: trama_ask
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Present a complete question round in the project's editor and wait for answers. Only an initial unavailable result permits your own question tool. An editor-interrupted error stops this workflow without fallback, retry, rerouting or resumption.

questions.description: All questions in this round, in presentation order.

recommended.description: Zero-based index of the recommended option.

languageModelTools.name: trama_view
languageModelTools.displayName: Trama: View the Model and Requirements
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Shows part of the project's Trama Model, the source of truth for how the software behaves, with the Requirements that say how it must be built. Without `ref`: the System, its Actors and Features. With `ref`: that element with its States, Transitions (condition and consequence in prose), Events, who receives them, and the Requirements attached to it. `requirements` lists the Requirement Areas; Requirements: `requirements/ui` (a whole Area) or `requirements/ui#order/Paid` (one section; `#General` for the general one). Element reference: `checkout` (Feature), `order` (Machine), `user` (Actor), `order/Paid` (State), `order/Paid/user.CANCEL` (Transitions on an Event), `user.CANCEL` (Event).

ref.description: Element reference: `checkout` (Feature), `order` (Machine), `user` (Actor), `order/Paid` (State), `order/Paid/user.CANCEL` (Transitions on an Event), `user.CANCEL` (Event). Or `requirements`, or Requirements: `requirements/ui` (a whole Area) or `requirements/ui#order/Paid` (one section; `#General` for the general one).

languageModelTools.name: trama_paths
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the simple paths between two States of one Machine, shortest first, with the Event and prose of each step.

languageModelTools.name: trama_analyze
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Warnings about the Model: unreachable States, non-final States with no way out, Events nobody receives. For one Machine or the whole System.

machine.description: Machine ID; omit for the whole System

languageModelTools.name: trama_search
languageModelTools.displayName: Trama: Search the Model and Requirements
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Case-insensitive search over names and prose of the whole Model and its Requirements; each hit with its reference.

languageModelTools.name: trama_board
languageModelTools.modelDescription: The work board: Draft Proposals in writing, handed-over (open) Proposals and Drifts waiting for the developer's decision, then Tasks to do, in progress and done.

languageModelTools.name: trama_validate
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks the internal consistency of the Model and its Requirements (every Requirement section must name an existing element), or of both with a Draft or open Proposal applied. Never looks at code.

proposal.description: Proposal ID; omit to validate the current Model

languageModelTools.name: trama_proposal_new
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Creates a Draft Proposal: the only way to change the Model or its Requirements. Write each changed Model or Requirement file with trama_proposal_write, then validate, review the changes and hand it over with trama_proposal_submit when finished. Only the developer can approve it after submission. A large change can be split into Proposals that build on each other: list the earlier ones in `requires`; this one is written and validated on top of them and can only be approved after them.

requires.description: IDs of Draft, open or approved Proposals this one builds on

import.description: True when the Proposal describes existing code (trama-import skill); approving it starts no Scan

languageModelTools.name: trama_proposal_write
languageModelTools.displayName: Trama: Write a Model or Requirement file in a Proposal
languageModelTools.userDescription: Write a Model or Requirement file in a Proposal
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Writes the complete new version of one Model or Requirement file inside a Draft or open Proposal (nothing changes until the developer approves). An open Proposal returns to Draft before the write; hand it over again with trama_proposal_submit when finished. `path`: Model file relative to `.trama/model/` (`checkout/order.md`, `actors/user.md`), or a Requirement Area `requirements/<area>.md`. Returns validation; a Requirement section naming a State the Proposal removes or renames is an error, so update that Requirement in the same Proposal.

path.description: Model file relative to `.trama/model/` (`checkout/order.md`, `actors/user.md`), or a Requirement Area `requirements/<area>.md`

content.description: The complete file in the Trama Model or Requirements format

languageModelTools.name: trama_proposal_delete_file
languageModelTools.displayName: Trama: Delete a Model or Requirement file in a Proposal
languageModelTools.userDescription: Delete a Model or Requirement file in a Proposal
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Marks a Model or Requirement file for deletion in a Draft or open Proposal. An open Proposal returns to Draft; hand it over again with trama_proposal_submit when finished. `path`: Model file relative to `.trama/model/` (`checkout/order.md`, `actors/user.md`), or a Requirement Area `requirements/<area>.md`.

path.description: Model file relative to `.trama/model/` (`checkout/order.md`, `actors/user.md`), or a Requirement Area `requirements/<area>.md`

languageModelTools.name: trama_proposal_submit
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Hands a Draft Proposal over to the developer, making it open for review. Call only after finishing every file, validating and reviewing the changes. Refuses invalid Model or Requirements and unregistered files, leaving it Draft; staleness and waiting for required approvals do not prevent submission.

languageModelTools.name: trama_proposal_show
languageModelTools.modelDescription: A Proposal: status, whether it is stale, its structural changes, validation, and the developer's feedback if it was rejected.

languageModelTools.name: trama_task_new
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Creates a Task in To do. A Task references the Model elements it implements in `refs`, plus any Requirement it must satisfy. A technical Task (no behaviour change) references no Model element, only Requirements if any. The body says in domain words what must be true when done.

refs.description: Model elements the Task covers, and Requirements it must satisfy. Element reference: `checkout` (Feature), `order` (Machine), `user` (Actor), `order/Paid` (State), `order/Paid/user.CANCEL` (Transitions on an Event), `user.CANCEL` (Event). Requirements: `requirements/ui` (a whole Area) or `requirements/ui#order/Paid` (one section; `#General` for the general one).

technical.description: True for work that changes no behaviour (refactor, dependencies, applying a Requirement); then refs may only name Requirements

drift.description: ID of the Drift this Task resolves, if any

proposal.description: ID of the Proposal (the design) this Task comes from, when you file it after that Proposal was approved; it must exist

body.description: What must be true when done, in domain words

languageModelTools.name: trama_task_show
languageModelTools.modelDescription: A Task with the current text of every Model element and Requirement it references, and the Requirements that apply to those elements. Says which Drifts, or which fix Task, block it.

languageModelTools.name: trama_task_move
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Moves a Task to `todo`, `doing` or `done`. Moving it to `doing` takes it: the developer cannot move it until the Task leaves `doing` or the developer takes it back. A blocked Task (an open Drift blocks it, or it waits for the Task that fixes its Drift) cannot be moved to `doing` by you: the move is refused and the Drift or Task is named. Move it to `doing` when you start and to `done` when the behaviour matches the Model and the code follows its Requirements.

languageModelTools.name: trama_drift_new
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Records a Drift: the code differs from the Model in a way that would change the Diagram, or contradicts a Requirement. File it exactly once. If the code handles an important case the Model forgot, first open a Proposal and pass its ID in `proposal`. Only the developer resolves Drifts.

refs.description: The Model elements or Requirements closest to the difference. Element reference: `checkout` (Feature), `order` (Machine), `user` (Actor), `order/Paid` (State), `order/Paid/user.CANCEL` (Transitions on an Event), `user.CANCEL` (Event). Requirements: `requirements/ui` (a whole Area) or `requirements/ui#order/Paid` (one section; `#General` for the general one).

proposal.description: ID of a Proposal that would fix the Model, if the code is right

task.description: ID of the Task you were implementing when you found the difference; leave out for a Scan or a Fix

body.description: What the code does, what the Model or Requirement says, where in the code

languageModelTools.name: trama_drift_show
languageModelTools.modelDescription: A Drift with its references, the Requirements that apply, and its attached Proposal, if any.
